intro: Lesson 100: Revision: Physics 3 light and sound. Answer every question. Show your working. Mark it with the mark scheme and log any errors in your repair list.

questions.a: Angle of incidence = angle of reflection

questions.q: Light entering glass bends... the normal.
Big question: how can light travel along a bent glass fibre?
questions.a: By total internal reflection: it hits the sides at more than the critical angle and reflects all the way along.

questions.q: Calculate the critical angle for water (n = 1.33).
questions.model: sin c = 1 ÷ n = 1 ÷ 1.33 = 0.752. Inverse sine: c = 48.8°.

questions.q: State two conditions for total internal reflection.
questions.a: Light travels from a denser to a less dense medium (1); angle of incidence greater than the critical angle (1).

questions.q: Describe how to find the refractive index of a glass block. Portal response box.
questions.a: Draw round block, mark normal (1); ray box to shine ray at measured angle i (1); mark emerging ray, join to find refracted ray (1); measure r with protractor (1); repeat for several i (1); calculate sin i ÷ sin r and average, or plot sin i against sin r (1).
questions.model: Teacher writes the first two points: 'Place the block on paper and draw round it. Draw a normal at 90° to one face where the ray will enter.'

questions.q: Explain how an optical fibre carries a signal round a bend.
questions.a: Light enters the fibre (1); hits the inside surface at more than the critical angle (1); is totally internally reflected repeatedly along the fibre (1).

questions.q: A clap echoes from a wall 85 m away after 0.5 s. Calculate the speed of sound.
